audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and 6 were scored Skill even though whys[3] says you keep the poke edge through 4-5 and whys[4] says a dashless Swain dies to the level-6 chain. The 2+ item row was scored Kennen while whys[6] says Swain reclaims it.
audit.why: 57.07% over 184 games is a clearly favoured lane that Kennen owns from level 2 to first item, and gives back only once soul stacks and Demonic Ascension scale.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 flipped to Kennen and row 6 to Swain, in matched pairs.

audit.why: Kennen's level-6 and Alternator/Rocketbelt windows land before Swain's soul-stack scaling, which is exactly what the spikes said.
audit.corrected: Demonic Ascension's 120s and Nevermove's 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 written in so the commit windows have numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vision of Empire is called his Q in three fields ('his Vision of Empire Q', 'Swain's Q-Vision-of-Empire', 'Stack Vision of Empire Q poke and W bombs'), and four fields say Nevermove 'cancels your R channel'.
audit.why: Death's Hand is Q — piercing bolts that stack damage per bolt, 750 range. Vision of Empire is W, the long-range eye (5500-7500 range, 22s) that reveals and grants him a Soul Fragment. And Slicing Maelstrom carries no channel flag, so a root does not switch it off; what Nevermove actually does is root you on the wave's RETURN trip and let Swain recast to pull you into his drain radius.
audit.corrected: Slots renamed, and the root restated as a return-trip root plus a pull into Demonic Ascension.
sources: enemyKit E text 'It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits'

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never explains why chip damage stops working.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock's Soul Fragments heal him and permanently raise his maximum health, so poke that is not backed by Grievous Wounds funds his scaling instead of denying it. Nevermove also has a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension, so the 12s window you commit on shrinks once he ults.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds timing stated in whys[5] and late; the shortened E cooldown during his ult noted in the notes for the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page tracks Demonic Ascension as the cooldown to engage on.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is 120s but persists indefinitely while he drains champions, so 'when it is down' is not a lane-trading rhythm. Nevermove at 12s is the ability whose cooldown actually gates your all-in — without the root he cannot hold you in the drain.
audit.corrected: Commit windows re-keyed to Nevermove in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t; Demonic Ascension kept as the fight-avoidance rule.

edits.before: Swain is immobile with no dash, which is exactly what your Q wants — chip him with Thundering Shuriken from max range and stack Electrical Surge autos he can't out-sustain pre-6. The one thing to respect is his E, Nevermove: it's a slow-traveling root that pulls you in, so never walk a straight line at him or eat it while stepping up for CS. At level 2-3, if he oversteps to land a W bomb or a Q, punish — he can't dodge your return poke and can't run from it.
edits.after: Swain is immobile with no dash, which is exactly what your Q wants — chip him with Thundering Shuriken from 950 and stack Electrical Surge autos he can't out-sustain pre-6. Respect Nevermove (E): the wave is harmless going out and roots on the way BACK, and he can then recast to drag you in, so never stand still in its return line. At level 2-3, if he oversteps to place Vision of Empire, punish — he can't dodge your poke and can't run from it.

edits.before: This is your window. By 6 your Slicing Maelstrom turns a clean all-in lethal: bait or sidestep his E pull, then E onto him, stack Mark of the Storm with W, and R to stun-lock — a dashless Swain can't escape the chain and your burst beats his drain before Demonic Ascension ramps. The discipline is the E: if Nevermove lands, it cancels your R channel and your E-in, so all-in only when it's on cooldown. Your Hextech Alternator/Rocketbelt spike is your peak — force the kill here.
edits.after: This is your window. By 6 your Slicing Maelstrom turns a clean all-in lethal: bait or sidestep his E, then E onto him, stack Mark of the Storm with W, and R to stun-lock — a dashless Swain can't escape the chain and your burst beats his drain before Demonic Ascension ramps. The discipline is the E: a landed Nevermove lets him pull you into his own drain radius, so all-in only on its 12s cooldown. Your Alternator/Rocketbelt spike is your peak — force the kill here.

edits.before: Win the lane on your 6/first-item spike, because late game tilts back toward Swain. Once he has Demonic Ascension up with soul stacks and Liandry's, an extended AOE fight feeds his R drain and out-sustains your short-cooldown burst, and a single landed E pull roots you out of your R channel. Don't sidelane-duel him into the late game — pivot to a teamfight engager, hold your R for his backline, and never face a fight where his drain gets to tick uninterrupted.
edits.after: Win the lane on your 6/first-item spike, because late game tilts back toward Swain. Once he has Demonic Ascension up with soul stacks and Liandry's, an extended AOE fight feeds his drain and out-heals your short-cooldown burst, and one landed Nevermove drags you into the middle of it. Buy Grievous Wounds before that: Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently raises his max HP, so unanswered chip funds him. Don't sidelane-duel him late.

notes: Vision of Empire was labelled Swain's Q in three fields — it is his W (5500-7500 range, 22s, grants him a Soul Fragment on champion hit); Q is Death's Hand. The 'Nevermove cancels your R channel' claim appeared four times and is not supportable: Slicing Maelstrom has no channel flag. The real interaction, now written in, is that Nevermove roots on the wave's RETURN and Swain recasts to pull you into his drain radius. One thing worth the user knowing that I only put in this note: Riot's text says Nevermove's cooldown is SHORTER during Demonic Ascension, so the 12s commit window you are counting shrinks the moment he ults — I did not state a number for it because the kit file gives none.
